strengths: Novel mechanistic interpretability approach to spatial relation generation in diffusion transformers, addressing an understudied aspect of T2I models
Well-motivated 'Attention Synopsis' method for analyzing massive attention tensors (10M+ maps) at scale—practical contribution for mechanistic interpretability research
Rigorous experimental design with controlled synthetic dataset, multiple model scales, and multiple text encoder configurations enabling clean comparisons

Comprehensive evidence for findings: attention patterns, QK/VO circuit analysis, ablations (L2H8 ablation: 67→33%, L4H3 ablation: 90→76%), causal interventions (VO injection), training dynamics, and variance partitioning
Clear contrast between RTE and T5 circuits with distinct mechanistic explanations (two-stage modular vs. information fusion)
Strong reproducibility: extensive appendices with pseudocode, hyperparameters, detailed methods, and commitment to release code/data
Honest acknowledgment of limitations and presentation of robustness findings (40% drop from perturbation) without overstating generality
weaknesses: Severe scope limitations undermine generalization claims: only 2 objects (real scenes have 5+), 8 directional relations only, tiny models (DiT-B is 12 layers), synthetic only, low resolution (128×128). Enormous gap to real T2I systems (DALL-E, Stable Diffusion); no empirical validation that findings transfer.

Main practical finding—'text encoders matter for spatial reasoning'—was already known from cited work [33, 17]. Mechanistic explanation is new but actionable insight is not. Suggestion that 'encoder improvements > DiT modifications' is speculative without real-model experiments.

T5-DiT mechanism incompletely explained: why does adding 'the' cause catastrophic failure (40% drop)? Variance partitioning shows relation info (~12-21%) is present, but how it's used downstream is unclear. Why don't RTE models suffer similarly?

Limited architectural exploration: only one architecture (PixArt), only two text encoders (T5, random). Real T2I uses diverse designs (CLIP, hybrids). Findings may be artifacts of PixArt rather than general properties.

Robustness evaluation too narrow: only one perturbation type tested (adding 'the'). Should test paraphrasing, synonyms, reordering. The 40% drop is isolated; no analysis of which components cause fragility.

QK circuit explanation lacks rigor: composite relation decomposition (Fig 4B) shown qualitatively; unclear if exact or approximate. 'Gradient tagging' analogy is informal; mathematical formalism needed.

Incomplete ablations: no hybrid models (RTE with T5-style fusion, vice versa), no attempts to improve T5-DiT robustness, limited lesioning studies. DiT-nano failure (5%) unexplained—capacity threshold?
Evaluation concerns: binary contour-detection metrics may miss spatial understanding; no human evaluation. Single injection example (Fig 5C) generalized without showing consistency across prompts.

strengths: Novel mechanistic interpretability approach to spatial reasoning in DiTs with methodological innovations (Attention Synopsis, weight-space screening, variance partitioning)
Rigorous experimental design with controlled synthetic dataset, multiple model sizes, and comprehensive ablations with strong causal evidence
Clear circuit discoveries contrasting modular (RTE) vs. integrated (T5) strategies for encoding spatial relations, with direct explanation of robustness differences
Practical finding that T5-based models are brittle to prompt perturbations while RTE-based models are stable, relevant for T2I deployment
Reproducible research with comprehensive methodological details and promised public release of code/datasets
Generalizes analysis across encoders (T5, CLIP) and attempts transfer to pre-trained models
weaknesses: Extremely limited scope: toy synthetic dataset (3 shapes, 2 colors, 8 relations, 128×128px, 2 objects, gray backgrounds) orders of magnitude simpler than real T2I prompts with no evidence of scalability
Poor transfer to real models: PixArt-Sigma analysis shows only 8/30 object pairs have meaningful spatial accuracy, undercutting claims about understanding real T2I systems
RTE baseline is artificial—no real models use random embeddings; comparison against realistic encoders with semantic structure would be more informative than RTE
Circular analysis methods: Attention Synopsis relies on knowing true labels; object evaluation uses brittle pixel thresholding; weight-space screening depends on correct variance factorization
Limited actionability: identifies T5 brittleness (40% accuracy drop) without proposing solutions or tested interventions to improve spatial robustness
Speculative extrapolation to real-world scenarios (Abstract/Intro) contradicted by weak pre-trained model performance; findings may not generalize beyond synthetic setting
No analysis of scalability to 3+ objects, complex relations (occlusion, 'between'), or natural language variation; missing statistical confidence intervals and error bars
Presentation: critical methods relegated to appendix; figures are small/dense; narrative could better prioritize key findings for venue
